trust_decision.summary: Source-derived strings (repo user/name from the src argument and the dest path) are interpolated into a shell command line passed to child_process.exec; the decision whether they are treated as data or shell syntax is made at the single exec primitive in src/utils.js, fed from _cloneWithGit and fetchRefs in src/index.js.

landing_point.why: README says --mode=git 'uses git under the hood'; an engineer reading 'command injection' greps for 'git clone' and lands on _cloneWithGit.

fix_sites.entry_point: exported utils exec (default for opts.exec), used by every route below
CLI `degit <src>` default tar mode, public API clone(), and degit.json `clone` directive (index.js:47-57) via _getHash -> _fetchRefs
parse() called from the Degit constructor for every src (CLI, API, interactive, degit.json directive)
fix_sites.module_kind: input parser (restructured; not itself the protection)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/utils.js:33 (exported exec, also the default for public opts.exec at src/index.js:38); plus tar-mode fetchRefs at src/index.js:371-373, which the git-mode-focused report does not point to

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Tar mode is the default 'download a tarball' path and fetchRefs only builds repo.url from a fixed https domain, so a solver can argue ls-remote is not the git-mode clone the report describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate repo identifiers must keep parsing and working: sourcehut users with '~' (e.g. ~satotake), underscores (Rich_Harris), dots/.git suffix, subdirs and #refs; dest paths with spaces; rm -rf of dest/.git after a git clone; opts.exec injection used by tests. An over-broad character blacklist in parse() or rejecting paths breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: dest argument (CLI positional, interactive prompt, API clone(dest))

O7_producer.where: src/index.js:76-84 loads degit.json from the downloaded template via tryRequire (src/utils.js:22-31); its clone action src flows to degit(action.src) at src/index.js:57 and on to fetchRefs exec at src/index.js:373

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A directive action (e.g. a git-mode clone or post-clone command) built from degit.json fields and run through a separate exec helper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: README advertises 'Additional actions may be added in future' and postinstall scripts as a planned capability; a maintainer could add one with its own child_process call in another file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Interactive mode rebuilding src from cache directory names / map.json keys and passing it to a git helper (e.g. refreshing refs) that shells out
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Interactive mode already reconstructs host:user/repo#ref from the ~/.degit cache; a cache refresh via git would be a natural feature and crosses a save/reload boundary.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fallback downloader in tar mode that shells out to git archive or curl when https fetch fails
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Proxy/private-host fallbacks are commonly requested; it would be a second implementation of fetching away from utils.exec.

O9_family: OS command injection (shell string interpolation into child_process.exec; CWE-77/78)

O10_build.project_tests: test/index.test.js (createMockExec git-mode and ls-remote cases, offline via opts.exec), test/utils.test.js (exec spy), test/helpers.js; test/live.test.js needs network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Switch the single exec helper to execFile with argument arrays (which closes every route at once), or tighten the parse() regex to reject shell metacharacters.

out_of_scope_notes: Argument injection (dest or src beginning with '-') into git clone/ls-remote remains after the first commit; the '--' separator appears only in a later tree and is not in this diff.
utils.fetch follows redirects to any Location without host checks (src/utils.js:80); separate concern.
